label: D1 after an unrewarded visit to S1
explanation: Fires only at D1 and only when the reward input is 0. Within that, it fires almost exclusively when the previous trial reached S1 (prev_state == -1 covers the first trial of a window, where the previous state is out of window; these are the remaining misses). It does not fire at GO or D2, after any rewarded trial, or after an unrewarded visit to S2. Read this way, it signals that S1 just failed to pay, which is evidence that S2 is good. Magnitude is largest when the agent is about to choose a2 and the hidden good state is S2 (top windows are all good=S2 with a2 choices; choice logit strongly toward a2). It is weak or silent when an S1 non-reward comes while the agent still favours a1 (good=S1), and these cases are the main false positives. Adding the agent-own upcoming choice action==2 for the out-of-window case raises dev F1 from 0.80 to 0.85. I recorded the simpler, purely observed predicate instead (dev P 0.67, R 0.997, mass recall 1.0).

issues: The basic claims hold. All activation mass is at D1; GO and D2 have 0 active steps. The feature never fires when prev_reward==1 (0 of 740k steps), and it almost never fires after an unrewarded visit to S2 (dev P 0.003, mass 0.00002).

The prev_state==-1 clause lowers F1. Dropping it gives dev F1 0.811 (P 0.80, R 0.82) and test F1 0.808, against 0.804 / 0.799 with it. On its own the clause has precision 0.39 and is the largest source of false positives. The clause only pays off when it is gated by the agent's upcoming choice: (prev_state==-1)&(action==2) has P 0.58, while (prev_state==-1)&(action==1) has P 0.15.

The explanation misplaces the systematic structure. Strength depends on how S1 was reached. Rare a2->S1 unrewarded: dev P 0.989, 75% of activation mass, and it covers 81% of the top two activation quartiles. Common a1->S1 unrewarded: P 0.56 but only 6% of mass, 71% of the lowest quartile and 0% of the top two quartiles. So the weak firings and false positives come from the previous choice being a1 (common transition), not mainly from good==S1 as the explanation claims. The explanation never mentions prev_action or prev_common, although prev_common==0 holds 75% of mass and prev_common==1 only 6%.

The label 'D1 after an unrewarded visit to S1' is fine as a binary description, but it hides that strong activations are specific to rare-unrewarded trials after an a2 choice. Those are the trials where a model-based agent should repeat a2. Unrewarded a1->S1 common visits barely activate the feature.

Test misses: 191 missed steps with 0.0% of the mass, so recall is fine. The 26,468 false positives are systematic: windows with prior a1->S1 common unrewarded, and first-trial windows where the agent then picks a1.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after an unrewarded S1 visit, strongest when S1 was reached rarely from a2 (an a2 repeat cue); weak after common a1->S1 non-reward
